subject: QBR bridge-plan: scope reductions, dependency asks & updated runbook
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>; Brandon Lee <brandon@catalysthealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR bridge-plan: scope reductions, dependency asks & updated runbook

Team — putting a short plan on your radar for the QBR and the OKR re-scope we've been iterating on. I ran the heatmap attached (Q4_OKR_heatmap.xlsx) and we need to do two things to keep the top-level objectives realistic for the quarter: tighten scope on the model-ops OKR and accelerate a small set of infra tickets that unlock latency/cost wins.

High-level proposal
- Cut non-critical telemetry surfaced to the console (approx 20% reduction in event volume) — target: remove by 10/18. Owner: Vanessa.
- Narrow rollout for kernel-batching to a single high-traffic customer cohort rather than org-wide. Owner: Karthik.
- Postpone low-risk quality experiments (A/B stems) until next quarter.

Critical dependencies we need signoff on this week
- SOC 2 evidence for Catalyst Health integration (we need their audit SLA confirmation by 10/06) — external: Brandon Lee (Catalyst).
- Priority infra tickets: SUP-425, SUP-431, SUP-437 — need infra allocation (estimate: 2 sprints). Owner: Markus / Infra.
- Billing/procurement: PO timing from Catalyst procurement to finalize dedicated capacity quote — OpsCloud procurement contact is in cc.

Ask (concrete)
1) Can Markus confirm if we can reassign 0.5 FTE from sustained-performance team for two sprints to close the three infra tickets? (answer by 10/04)
2) Vanessa/Karthik: confirm whether the narrow kernel-batching rollout covers Catalyst's traffic pattern (quick thumbs by 10/03).
3) Brandon/Procurement: confirm PO timeline and whether Catalyst can accept a slightly delayed A/B experiment window (confirm by 10/06).

I propose a QBR dry-run on 10/12 10:00 PT where we present the reduced-scope narrative and the updated runbook (runbook_update.md). If we can't hit the infra tickets, we'll flag a contingency plan (fallback to smaller quantization change).

Thanks — will consolidate replies and publish a short action tracker.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Product Strategy, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

Attachments: Q4_OKR_heatmap.xlsx

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR bridge-plan: scope reductions, dependency asks & updated runbook

Irene — thanks for the clear ask and the heatmap. I'm supportive of the narrower rollout; keeping the kernel-batching to a single cohort is the right trade for latency predictability.

Quick clarifications:
- When you say "latency/cost wins" for the infra tickets, are we targeting p95 latency or average token latency? That affects how we prioritize SUP-431.
- 0.5 FTE for two sprints is likely doable, but I need Karthik to confirm that shifting focus won't block the quantization work we're running in parallel. If Karthik thumbs up, I'll route the allocation through the infra planner and assign a delivery owner by 10/04.

Markus
VP, Platform Engineering
markus@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR bridge-plan: scope reductions, dependency asks & updated runbook

Irene / Markus — short update from Product Ops and Delivery perspective: we can absorb the narrower rollout and deprioritize the A/B stems this quarter. On the infra tickets: delivery can commit 2 sprints but that means we will push the third-party SDK work (ticket SUP-442) to next quarter.

I created a slim runbook draft and pushed notes to the shared folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQBRPrep). I've attached the runbook update (runbook_update.md) with the proposed rollback points and owner matrix.

Action notes:
- Laura: will own release coordination, approve rollback windows by 10/08.
- Vanessa: please confirm telemetry reduction checklist by 10/18 (this is the gating item for cost savings).
- Karthik: can you confirm kernel-batching will not regress cache hit rates for Catalyst (10/03)?

I'll also raise SUP-425/431/437 in the weekly infra sync and ask for sprint-level assignments.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations
laura@redwood.com

Attachment: runbook_update.md

From: Brandon Lee <brandon@catalysthealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: OpsCloud Procurement <procurement@opscloud.io>
Date: 2026-10-04T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR bridge-plan: scope reductions, dependency asks & updated runbook

Irene — thanks for the heads-up and the clear asks. From Catalyst's side: we can accept the narrower kernel-batching rollout and the proposed delay of the low-risk A/B experiments. Our compliance team is finishing the SOC 2 evidence review and I can confirm we can provide the items you requested by 10/06. I'm attaching a draft QBR slide input (QBR_input_Catalyst.docx) with metrics and the customer success perspective.

Procurement note: I've looped in our procurement vendor (OpsCloud) — procurement@opscloud.io — who will follow up with a PO timeline. We expect the PO to be approved the week of 10/11; if you need earlier confirmation for Dedicated capacity, tell us and we'll see if we can expedite.

Best,
Brandon Lee
VP Partnerships, Catalyst Health
brandon@catalysthealth.com

Attachment: QBR_input_Catalyst.docx

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Brandon Lee <brandon@catalysthealth.com>, OpsCloud Procurement <procurement@opscloud.io>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR bridge-plan: scope reductions, dependency asks & updated runbook — summary & owners

Thanks, everyone — consolidating decisions and owners so we have a single source of truth before the dry-run.

Decisions taken
- Narrow kernel-batching rollout approved (single cohort) — reduces risk and keeps the performance uplift for targeted customers.
- Telemetry reduction approved as primary cost lever; Vanessa to publish checklist.
- Infra tickets SUP-425/431/437 are prioritized for two-sprint delivery; delivery owner to be assigned by Markus.
- Catalyst will provide SOC 2 evidence by 10/06 and a QBR input deck (received). Procurement expects PO the week of 10/11.

Action tracker (owner / due)
- Markus: confirm infra delivery owner and whether 0.5 FTE reallocation is feasible — due 2026-10-04 (status: assigned, owner to be named in infra sync).
- Karthik: confirm kernel-batching impact on Catalyst cache hit distribution — due 2026-10-03 (status: confirmed).
- Vanessa: telemetry reduction checklist and implementation plan — due 2026-10-18.
- Laura: finalize release runbook and rollback windows (runbook_update.md) — due 2026-10-08.
- Brandon/Catalyst: SOC 2 artifacts and PO timing — SOC 2 by 2026-10-06, PO week of 2026-10-11.

Next steps:
- QBR dry-run: 2026-10-12 10:00 PT (30–45m). Please mark calendars; I will circulate a 2-slide narrative (scope rationale + contingency) by 10/09.
- If infra ownership looks risky in the infra sync today, we will fallback to smaller quantization ops; Laura will note contingency in the runbook.

Thanks all — I'll update the HubSpot deal (DEAL-3091) and share the final QBR narrative.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Product Strategy, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/3091
